A1.justification: Both complete 13-page PDFs describe the same RASO work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendix A.1 are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments and ablations in Tables 2–4 and Figure 4, plus a clinician evaluation of generated annotations in Appendix A.1 and Table 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original recognition experiments, ablations, video inference measurements, and clinician annotation evaluation.

M1.justification: The architecture, temporal fusion, training procedure, inference, and annotation pipeline are unchanged. Section 4.2 changes 'three parts' to 'four parts' but retains the same three component descriptions; it introduces no identifiable method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WebSurg-derived training data and CholecT50, Cholec80, GraSP, and EndoVis18 RSS evaluations. Image/video recognition tasks and the appendix clinician evaluation retain the same coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains CLIP, BiomedCLIP, PubMedCLIP, and SurgVLP; Table 3 retains Tripnet, Attention Tripnet, and Rendezvous. Figure 1's RAM/GPT-4o comparisons and the video comparison methods are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Benchmark sample counts, metrics, threshold selection, model configurations, and training budgets are identical. Appendix A.1 still evaluates 1,000 sampled images using seven clinicians.

E4.justification: The fine-tuning, pretraining, and temporal-fusion ablations in Section 5.3 are unchanged, as are the image-versus-video comparison and the appendix assessment of GPT-4o annotation quality.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The appendix agreement-rate estimation and reporting are identical.

E6.justification: All result entries and findings in Tables 2–5 and Figures 1 and 4 are retained. For example, supervised image recognition remains 57.5 mAP and video recognition remains 61.3 mAP; clinician agreement rates are unchanged.

T1.justification: Feature-tensor definitions in Section 3.1 and the agreement-rate definition in Appendix A.1 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The scientific contributions remain open-set surgical recognition, temporal fusion, scalable weak supervision, and improved benchmark performance. Their scope and claimed performance gains are unchanged; the resource-release statement changes under D1.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning temporal context, label-merging effects, pretraining benefits, annotation complementarity, and broader applicability are unchanged. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future promise to release code, model, and dataset with a statement that code, model, and demo are available at a project URL. This adds concrete access information, but the PDFs do not establish dataset release or verify the linked resources. Implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to RAM, surgical segmentation models, vision-language models, and surgical recognition methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited edits correct the abstract's 'gatherers to' wording and pluralize 'surgical actions.' Section 4.2 changes 'three parts' to 'four parts,' creating an inconsistency with its three named components. Section organization and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 fixes Table 5's caption/header overlap by moving the table downward and corrects 'Reconigtion' in Figure 1. The abstract also reflows around the new resource link. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The new resource-access information and repaired Table 5 spacing modestly improve usability, while the scientific evidence remains unchanged. The unsupported switch to 'four parts' in Section 4.2 introduces a small clarity regression, limiting the overall gain.
